div.head: PREFACE.
div.p: The present list is intended to include all birds which have been so far proven to occur in British Columbia.

I am fully aware of its incompleteness, and very much regret much of its lack of more definite information regarding the distribution of certain species, and with regard to that portion of the Province in north and northeastern interior, which, I have no doubt, is a valuable field for work.

Since the publication of the list of British Columbia birds in 1898 by the late John Fannin, which contained 339 species and sub-species, and with the information to hand, enables me to add to this 24.

I wish to extend my thanks especially to the following constant observers for more or less extended local lists, notes and specimens:—A. C. Brooks, Chilliwhack, Okanagan and Cariboo; Rev. J. H. Keen, Queen Charlotte Islands and Metlakatla; Thos. Kermode, William Head Quarantine Station; E. P. Venables, Yernon; Chas. de Blois Green, Fairview and Keremeos.
I have also obtained valuable information from the check-list published by the late John Fannin.

div.head: 105.PECTORAL SANDPIPER.
div.p: Not common; taken along the coast during migrations. Brooks has taken it at Chillihwack and Okanagan.

div.head: 106.BAIRD'S SANDPIPER.
div.p: Distributed along the coast of Island and Mainland, Rev. J. H. Keen reports it rare at Metlakatla. Taken at Chilliwhack and Okanagan (Brooks); and at Clover Point, Victoria (E. M. Anderson).

div.head: 108.RED-BACKED SANDPIPER.
div.p: Common in the spring and autumn migration along the coast of Island and Mainland. Brooks has taken it at Chilliwhack.

div.head: 109.SEMIPALMATED SANDPIPER.
div.p: Not uncommon in migration along the Coast. Chilliwhack and Okanagan. (Brooks.) Common at Metlakatla. (Rev. J. H. Keen.)

div.head: 110.WESTERN SEMIPALMATED SANDPIPER.
div.p: Abundant in the fall along the Coast. I also found it very common at Clayoquot, May, 1894, and have taken it near Victoria in July. Brooks has taken it at Chilliwhack.

div.head: 111.SANDERLING.
div.p: Not common; several have been taken near Victoria by A. H. Maynard. Brooks has taken it at Chilliwhack. Fairly common at Metlakatla. (Rev J. H. Keen.)

div.head: 112.MARBLED GODWIT.
div.p: The whole of British Columbia; breeds chiefly east of Cascades. (Fannin.) Port Simpson. (W. B. Anderson.)

div.head: 113.GREATER YELLOW-LEGS.
div.p: Common along the coast in winter; have taken it at Clayoquot in May. Brooks has taken it at Chilliwhack and Okanagan. I found it breeding around the lakes at Clinton, May, 1891. (Fannin.)

div.head: 114.LESSER YELLOW-LEGS.
div.p: Tolerably common through the Province; winters on the coast. Brooks has taken it at Chilliwhack and Okanagan.

div.head: 115.SOLITARY SANDPIPER.
div.p: Found throughout the Province. Taken at Chilliwhack and Okanagan. (Brooks).

div.head: 122.LONG-BILLED CURLEW.

div.p: Abundant along the entire coast of Island and Mainland. Breeds throughout its range. Common on Queen Charlotte Islands, at Skidegate.

div.head: 132.MOUNTAIN PARTRIDGE.

div.head: 143.COLUMBIAN SHARP-TAILED GROUSE. PRAIRIE CHICKEN.

div.head: 144.SAGE GROUSE.

div.head: 145.RING-NECKED PHEASANT.
div.p: Abundant on Vancouver Island and in the Lower Fraser River Valley and other portions of the Mainland. Introduced from China; now thoroughly naturalised.

div.head: 146.BAND-TAILED PIGEON.

div.head: 147.PASSENGER PIGEON.
div.p: Mentioned in John Keast Lord's "Naturalist in British Columbia" (1866). If it ever did occur here, it is now, without doubt, extinct. (Fannin.)

div.p: In September, 1880, I saw two of these birds at Burrard Inlet. It is more than probable they are accidental visitants here. Lord says: Mouth of Fraser River; seldom visits the Interior. (Fannin.)

div.head: 163.PRAIRIE FALCON.

div.head: 164.DUCK HAWK.

div.head: 170.AMERICAN OSPREY. FISH HAWK.
div.p: Common throughout the Province, on Mainland and Island, including Queen Charlotte Islands. Their nest is a huge heap of sticks, usually on the broken top of a tree.

div.head: 171.AMERICAN LONG-EARED OWL.
div.p: Not common; a few have been taken on Vancouver Island. Mr. Brooks has taken it at Chilliwhack and Okanagan.

div.head: 172.SHORT-EARED OWL.

div.head: 173.NORTHERN SPOTTED OWL.

div.head: 175.RICHARDSON'S OWL.
